description: A question is a specific kind of post; question rows form a subset of the post rows distinguished by the post type discriminator.
An answer is a specific kind of post; answer rows form a subset of the post rows distinguished by the post type discriminator.

connection_condition: An answer points at the question it belongs to through the parent post reference on its own post row.
description: Answers are component parts of the question they respond to and cannot be interpreted without their parent question.

connection_condition: A comment carries the identifier of the post it annotates.
description: Comments are attached parts of a post and lose their meaning without the annotated post.

connection_condition: A vote carries the identifier of the post it was cast on.
description: Votes are attached parts of a post; every vote belongs to exactly one post.

connection_condition: A revision carries the identifier of the post it changed.
description: Revisions are component parts of a post's history and cannot exist without the post they document.

connection_condition: A post's owner identifier refers to a user account, but may also be absent, in which case only a label remains.
description: Users own the posts they publish. No post identifier is stored on the user side, so this is a reference from content to person rather than containment.

connection_condition: A badge award carries the identifier of the user who received it.
description: Badge awards are attached to a user and have no meaning without the user who earned them.

connection_condition: Both attributes are stored on the same user row and describe the same account; the identifier is the key and the display name is the label recorded in the same catalogue.
description: Analytical questions name a person by display name while activity tables reference the numeric identifier, so the two representations denote the same user and must be reconciled.
A user's badge count is derived by counting that user's badge award records, optionally restricted to a named badge.
Post popularity is derived from readership, which the platform records as the view count of a question; comparing popularity means comparing this measure.
A user's influence is derived from accumulated reputation, so the most influential user is the one with the greatest reputation.
The elder-user category is derived from the declared age of a user by applying a senior-age threshold.
A post percentage is derived from post counts: the conditional count of posts meeting a stated condition over a stated denominator population.

connection_condition: Tag names embedded in a question's delimited tag list correspond to names in the tag catalogue, but the list is stored inline rather than as references.
description: Tag membership of a question and the tag catalogue describe the same topics through different representations, one denormalised and one catalogue-based.

connection_condition: Posts owned by the Community account are marked by a community-owned timestamp on the post row.
description: The Community account holds ownership of community-wiki content on behalf of the platform, so content attributed to it has no human author.

connection_condition: The label-only author columns are populated when no user identifier is recorded; synthesised account names also exist inside the user catalogue itself.
description: A display name recorded without a user identifier cannot be resolved to a person, yet it draws from the same textual name space as registered display names.
